accuracyFlags.claim: Section 05: 'the default open road limit varies by state, from 100 in most to 110 on many highways and 130 on specified Northern Territory sections' mixes default and posted limits.
accuracyFlags.correct: With no speed sign, the limit outside built-up areas is 100 km/h in NSW, Vic, Qld, SA, Tas and ACT, and 110 km/h in WA and NT. Some highways in other states are signposted 110. NT 130 km/h applies only on signposted sections of the Stuart, Barkly, Victoria and Arnhem highways. (NT pages returned 403 to the checker; NT detail from search summaries of official pages.)
accuracyFlags.fix: Sec 05 speed limits: default rural 100 km/h NSW/Vic/Qld/SA/Tas/ACT, 110 km/h WA and NT; 110 elsewhere only where signed; NT 130 only on signed sections (Main Roads WA, nt.gov.au) - low severity

notes: Page has no signs imagery, which is the dominant intent for 'road signs australia' (pos 64), so image search is lost. Overlaps with australia-road-rules-state-differences. Spanish version gets 59 impr but English 48 at pos 20.8 and 0 clicks.
accuracyFlagsOriginal: Road train signs described as 'a yellow ROAD TRAIN or LONG VEHICLE panel': check wording against state road-authority guidance; panel colours and rules differ by state.
'Default open road limit ... 100 in most to 110 ... 130 on specified NT sections' has no source; verify per state (NT 130 applies only to nominated highway sections).
No official source section (Austroads / state road authority), despite being a road-rules page; no images of the signs themselves.

Footer blurb says 'Find 74,000+ Australian places offline': AussieCamps is not an offline map; only place details and guides work offline, and the 74,000 total is out of scope but the wording should say 'place details and guides work offline'.
rejectedFlags: Road train 'yellow panel': correct per NHVR VSG-19 (consider softening 'not a roadside instruction').
No official source section / no images: page has a 'Check before you go' block; images are an SEO gap.
Footer '74,000+ places offline': accurate offline claim; 73,945 rows so '74,000+' slightly overstates.
